## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D 1v1 Rocket League-style game against a bot, first to 3 goals.

## Requirements
- User requested a finished game immediately and asked not to ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone Three.js arena game with a 3-minute cap, keyboard and touch controls, boost, jump, CPU opponent, scoreboard, pause, and rematch.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` implementing the game and responsive interface.
- Verified `node --check game.js` passes and viewed desktop/mobile browser screenshots.

### Active
- Mobile menu screenshot showed the game/menu rendering; recent CSS adjustments to HUD placement and touch control visibility were not yet visually checked during active gameplay.
- A local HTTP server and Playwright browser session were started for testing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload and verify mobile gameplay HUD no longer overlaps touch controls.
2. Check gameplay/pause/rematch behavior and fix any issues.
3. Finish with a brief summary, assumptions, and verification notes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, physics, bot AI, controls, match logic, UI updates.
- `index.html`: Game canvas, scoreboard, overlays, controls, UI.
- `style.css`: Arena game UI and responsive mobile layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; repo status showed the new game files as untracked.
- Desktop screenshot: `screenshots/arena.png`; mobile gameplay/menu screenshots: `screenshots/mobile-playing.png`, `screenshots/mobile-menu.png`.
- The mobile menu screenshot showed HUD artifacts beneath the overlay; touch controls are hidden for menu/pause/end via `updateUI()`, and boost/speed HUD were repositioned upward, but active gameplay after those changes still needs checking.

## Objective
- Complete a playable 3D 1v1 Rocket League-style game against a bot, first to 3 goals.

## Requirements
- Finish without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Use a standalone Three.js arena game with a 3-minute cap, keyboard and touch controls, boost, jump, CPU opponent, scoreboard, pause, and rematch.
- Reduce rendering cost for software WebGL by disabling shadows and antialiasing, capping pixel ratio at 1.25, removing point lights, and switching arena materials to Lambert.
- Raise the frame delta cap from `.035` to `.12` to reduce slow game timing at low frame rates.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game, responsive interface, controls, match logic, and overlays in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passes; browser console showed no errors.
- Verified mobile menu hides touch controls and the HUD; starting a match reveals controls and HUD.
- Verified keyboard driving increases the speed display, pause hides controls/HUD, and resume restores them.
- Earlier mobile screenshots confirmed HUD and touch controls do not overlap.

### Active
- Validate touch input and end-of-match/rematch flow; inspect visual quality after rendering changes.
- Continue assessing software-WebGL performance and match timing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test touch controls, end overlay, and rematch/restart behavior in the browser.
2. Recheck match-clock pacing and visual quality after the performance changes.
3. Finish with a brief summary, assumptions, and verification notes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, physics, bot AI, controls, match logic, and rendering changes.
- `index.html`: Game canvas, scoreboard, overlays, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Arena UI and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; game files remain untracked.
- SwiftShader/software-rendered mobile viewport testing measured about 9.7–9.9 FPS; game play and clock continue, but performance and pacing still need review.
